strategies.name: Sequential All-Reduce with Intermediate Scaling
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce operations with local element-wise scaling operations between each all-reduce. Uses 8 all-reduce dispatches with full W*S tensor payload each time. Represents the baseline reference pattern: straightforward serialization with no fusion or overlap, trading dispatch count for simplicity.

strategies.name: Fused Scale-Reduce with Pre-computed Coefficients
strategies.desc: Pre-computes all scale/unscale coefficients for all 8 stages into lookup tables, then fuses scaling operations into single vectorized passes before each all-reduce. Uses 8 all-reduce dispatches but reduces local computation overhead by batching coefficient applications and eliminating redundant clone() operations through in-place updates where safe.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Chain per Stage
strategies.desc: Replaces each all-reduce with a reduce-scatter (producing S-sized chunks) followed by local scaling on the owned shard, then all-gather to reconstruct the full tensor. Uses 16 collective dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but with smaller per-dispatch payloads (W*S / W = S for RS, growing back to W*S for AG), trading dispatch count for reduced per-rank communication volume in the scatter phase.

strategies.name: Pipelined Chunked All-Reduce with Stage Batching
strategies.desc: Partitions the W*S tensor into C chunks and pipelines all-reduce operations across chunks, allowing computation (scaling) on chunk i+1 to overlap with communication on chunk i. Uses 8*C all-reduce dispatches on smaller payloads (W*S/C each), representing a latency-vs-bandwidth tradeoff that hides computation in communication overlap.

strategies.name: Two-Level Hierarchical All-Reduce with Node-Local Aggregation
strategies.desc:
Exploits multi-node topology by performing intra-node all-reduce first (lower latency), then inter-node all-reduce, applying scale factors only at node boundaries to reduce arithmetic operations. Uses 16 collective dispatches (8 stages × 2 levels) but with asymmetric payload sizes, leveraging fast node-local interconnect to amortize the higher dispatch count.
